'''Ailsa Macgregor Keating''' is a mathematician specialising in [[symplectic geometry]] and [[homological mirror symmetry]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/profile/ailsa-keating/ | title=Ailsa Keating – European Women in Mathematics }}</ref> She is a professor in the Department of Pure Mathematics and Mathematical Statistics at the [[University of Cambridge]].

==Education and career==
Keating grew up in [[Toulouse]], France.{{r|about}} She read mathematics in [[Clare College, Cambridge]] from 2005 to 2009, earning a master's degree through [[Part III of the Mathematical Tripos]].{{r|glass}} She went on to graduate study at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]], completing her dissertation in 2014 with the dissertation ''Symplectic properties of Milnor fibres'' supervised by [[Paul Seidel]].{{r|mg}}

She returned to Cambridge as a Junior Research Fellow in [[Trinity College, Cambridge|Trinity College]] in 2014,{{r|glass}} at the same time doing postdoctoral research as a [[Simons Foundation]] Junior Fellow<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 16, 2026 |title=Simons Society of Fellows- Ailsa Keating |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/people/ailsa-keating/ |url-status=live |website=Simons Foundation}}</ref> at [[Columbia University]] and a member of the [[Institute for Advanced Study]]. She became a lecturer at Cambridge in 2017{{r|about}} and was promoted to professor in 2023.{{r|dpmms}}

==Recognition==
Keating is the winner of the 2021 [[Berwick Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]], for her research using [[Dehn twist]]s to study the symmetries of [[symplectic manifold]]s.{{r|berwick}}
